data.name: Dipak
data.gender_notes: Dipak is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Dipak is derived from the Sanskrit word 'deep' which means 'a lamp' or 'a light'. In Hindu mythology, Dipak is the name of the god Agni, who is the god of fire. It is believed that Agni is the eternal light that illuminates the path to the gods and the universe. Dipak represents courage, knowledge, and wisdom. The name Dipak carries the meaning “Lamp, Light” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dipak usually hope their child will grow to embody lamp, light and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Dipak belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lamp, Light.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dipak total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

vedic_reference.note: The name Dipak is derived from the Sanskrit word 'दिप्' (dip), which means 'light'. In Hindu mythology, Dipak is the name of the celestial lamp that is carried by the god Agni, the god of fire. Dipak is also the name of a constellation in the northern hemisphere, which is believed to represent the celestial lamp. The name Dipak is often given to babies as a symbol of enlightenment and knowledge.

historical_references.reference: Dipak is a Sanskrit name meaning 'radiant, shining, glowing lamp'. It is considered an auspicious name in Hinduism, often given to boys as a name for a child born during Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights.
The god Dhanvantari, who is considered the embodiment of Ayurveda, is often depicted carrying a staff topped with a lamp, named Dipak. This lamp symbolizes the power of knowledge and healing.
